findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a file on the instance. User data can be retrieved by processes/users with instance access and may be exposed through cloud control-plane or instance metadata access paths, disclosing database credentials.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security group limits inbound access to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to an internet-routable interface and expands attack surface.

The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and associated snapshots are not encrypted at rest. Compromise or unauthorized access to underlying stored data can expose database contents.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to 0.0.0.0/0. It allows a compromised database instance to communicate freely with arbitrary external hosts, enabling data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic.

The EC2 application role is granted all S3, EC2, and RDS actions against every resource. A compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would provide broad account-level control and data access.
